subject: Performance gap mapping & action plan for AtlasHealth

Subject: Performance gap mapping & action plan for AtlasHealth

Hi Sara / John —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side so we have shared context and clear next steps. I focused this note on concrete gaps vs your stated goals so we can prioritize a short proof-of-concept.

Key pain points you called out
- Initial-response latency (streaming first-token p95) is inconsistent: current p95 ~420ms on your prod-like trace; target is <= 200ms for interactive clinician workflows.
- Sustained throughput for batch inference spikes: peak burst to ~800 RPS for short windows (~10–30s) but system backpressure and queuing increases tail latency.
- Multiplexed streaming UX drops frames under concurrency >150 streams; users see stutter and partial outputs.
- Operational friction: tricky to reproduce workload locally (Triton + k8s + custom proxy), and no consistent KV-cache across pods.

What you shared about stack and constraints
- Models served on-prem via Triton (NVIDIA) behind a homegrown gateway; models are int8-quantized variants of a 7B+ family. Typical prompt length ~120 tokens, expected output ~60 tokens.
- Network topology: internal VPC + VPN from clinics; extra 30–60ms of network RTT to inference cluster in peak hours.
- Security: must not send PHI outside VPC during pilot; we discussed a private deployment option.

Success criteria (proposed)
1) Streaming first-token p95 <= 200ms for 95% of requests under a 200 concurrent stream baseline.
2) Sustained 800 RPS for 30s bursts with p95 of token latency < 350ms (system can degrade gracefully).
3) No frame drops / partial-output events under 150 concurrent users.
4) Reproducible benchmark run & acceptance checklist to sign off PoC.

Proposed next steps (we talked about these on the call)
- AtlasHealth: share anonymized perf logs + a small representative request sample (CSV).
- Redwood: run a baseline run in our isolated cluster (private trial) using your sample; deliver a gap map showing where p95 and throughput exceed targets.
- Joint: schedule a 90-minute engineering sync (trial design + ingress) the week of Nov 29.
- Procurement: Marissa will send a short MAP and trial SOW for review.

I've attached two small artifacts: a CSV sample mapping (atlashealth-metrics-sample.csv) you sent during the call and a draft MAP with MOP rows for sign-off.

Attachment stubs: [Attachment: atlashealth-metrics-sample.csv (text/csv, 18KB)], [Attachment: MAP-AtlasHealth-20261122.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 42KB)]

Open questions / clarifications for your team
- Can we run with a copy of model binaries in a controlled private trial (no external network) or do you need us to deploy next to your cluster?
- Are there hard SLAs around request retries or do you prefer graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model) when concurrency spikes?

Thanks — I kept this intentionally focused so we can move quickly.

Best,

Thanks Sofia — this is exactly the level of detail that helps. A few quick clarifications: 

• We can export anonymized logs (no PHI) and have a small sample of the gateway traces. I attached the CSV you referenced.
• On deployment: preferred is a private trial inside our environment (we want to avoid outbound model copies). If that's not possible we can provide a secure VPN endpoint for a Redwood-managed cluster.
• Retrying behavior: our clinicians expect low-latency responses and retries complicate UX — prefer graceful degradation (fallback to faster model) over transparent retries for now.

Procurement note: we need an estimate for the trial SOW (duration, cost, support level). Marissa/Ben — can you share the MAP and a draft SOW we can present to procurement this week?

Sara Knox

AtlasHealth

Sara — thanks for the quick reply. Per your procurement ask, I've sketched a short MAP and draft SOW; attaching the MAP (spreadsheet) and an estimated SOW summary inline below.

SOW (trial) — summary
- Duration: 3 weeks (engineering validation + 1 full benchmark run + acceptance window)
- Scope: private trial deployment (customer-managed VPC or Redwood-managed private cluster), baseline profiling, two optimization passes (batching + KV caching), rolling smoke test with your tracer, and a final gap report.
- Support: 2x Redwood SEs for 3 weeks, 1x on-call during benchmark run.
- Estimated cost: USD 35,000 (pilot professional services + reserved trial infra).

MAP highlights (from the attached worksheet)
- Milestone 1: Data & artifacts delivered (logs + model binary access method) — due Nov 25
- Milestone 2: Trial deployment & baseline run — Dec 1–3
- Milestone 3: Optimizations & second run — Dec 6–8
- Milestone 4: Acceptance report & MOP sign-off — Dec 10

If you want a lower-cost option, we can reduce scope to a bench-only engagement where Atlas provides a secure model copy to Redwood; estimated cost ~USD 12,000. That would not include on-prem orchestration.
